newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Kiwi dollar holds gains at close, stays well bid.
newsitem.headline: Kiwi dollar holds gains at close, stays well bid.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar held onto its gains in sluggish Tuesday trade to end fairly much on its opening level.
The kiwi closed at US$0.6901/08, against its 0.6903/10 open and 0.6892/99 finish on Monday.
It traded a 0.6897-13 range during the session.
"It's been pretty slow. In fact even the U.S. dollar against the yen has been quiet today," a Wellington dealer said.
The soft dollar/yen was responsible for keeping the New Zealand dollar's Trade-Weighted Index (TWI) soft.
The TWI ended at 67.21 from 67.28 on Monday's close and 67.47 at the end of last week.

The Reuters Monetary Conditions Index fell through -1.0 again during the session, meaning conditions were more than 100 basis points (in interest rate terms) easier than the Reserve Bank's desired level. The index came back to end at 0.99.
Dealers said the market was prepared to buy the kiwi on any dips in the lead-up to the various eurokiwi settlements due over the next two or three weeks.
However, traders were likely to exit any built-up long positions by the end of the month, with the government's budget due on June 26 and the Reserve Bank's Monetary Policy Statement on June 27.
